title: fix(core): report a bare-name collision at both registry doors, across both tables
body:
Fixes #9821

Clause-②: no

`Registry.registerLazy` took the same `namespace && !skipFallback` bare-name fallback branch as `register` with no collision check at all. The repair is not the obvious one, and the census is what decided its shape.

## 1. The falsification came first, and triage's inference SURVIVED it

The dispatch's first task: read objectui#9533's reproduction and determine whether its two lazy declarations are the two console files, a third-party package, or a fixture.

**They are the two console files.** Three sources agree, and I took the third myself:

| source | reading |
|---|---|
| objectui#9533's body table | `apps/console/src/preview-gallery.tsx:36` and `apps/console/src/register-plugins.ts:65`, both `registerLazy`, both `plugin-dashboard:dashboard`; the third claimant is `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/index.tsx:79`, `register`, `view:dashboard` |
| the reproduction's own transcript, quoted in PR objectui#9803's body | a fresh `Registry` fed the package's real declared metadata, labelled `=== fresh Registry, stub then eager (what the console does) ===`, ending `=== collision warnings seen === 0`. The probe file itself was deleted by that delivery, so the transcript is the durable artefact |
| my own re-take, `origin/main` `26ac5036`, 2026-09-18T08:15Z | `node scripts/check-registry-bare-name-collisions.mjs --json` reports the `dashboard` group with exactly those three claimants, at those files and lines |

⇒ triage's inference holds: **copying the existing guard into `registerLazy` would not have caught the card that produced this one.** Both lazy claimants declare ONE full type, so a lazy-vs-lazy comparison excuses them, and the contest is against the *other* table.

## 2. The cross-table census — taken first, because it decides which table the predicate keys on

All readings on `origin/main` `26ac5036`, taken 2026-09-18T08:15Z. **PR objectui#9803 had NOT landed** (re-checked at 08:31Z: open, draft, unmerged, head `588e4595`), so the `dashboard` contest is still live on the tree these numbers describe. That PR does not touch `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts`; it does touch the collision gate I used as an instrument, which is why the ref and time are on every row.

| reading | value |
|---|--:|
| registration claims in shipped source | **425** (385 `register` / 40 `registerLazy`) |
| distinct bare keys claimed | **237** |
| bare keys claimed by at least one lazy stub | **31** |
| …of those, also claimed by an eager registration | **31 / 31** (no bare key is stub-only) |
| …naming ONE full type across both tables (the ordinary lifecycle) | **30** |
| …contested across the tables, different full types | **1** — `dashboard` |
| lazy-vs-lazy contests (two stubs, different full types) | **0** |
| bare keys stubbed twice, same full type, different loader closure | **9** |
| guarded placeholder claims overlapping a lazy stub's bare key | **0** — control: 84 guarded claims are visible to the same query and all 84 intersect the full bare-key set, so the zero is a reading and not a blind instrument |

The dynamic half, replaying those 425 declared claims against a real `Registry` (temporary probe, since deleted):

| order | before | after |
|---|--:|--:|
| A — all stubs, then all eager registrations (**the real boot order**) | **0** warnings | **1** |
| B — all eager registrations, then all stubs (the reverse) | **0** | 2 (one contest, reported by each of the two console files) |
| C — declaration order as the gate reads the tree | **0** | **1** |
| control: two eager registrations, one bare key, different full types | 1 | 1 |
| control: the same pair with `skipFallback: true` | 0 | 0 |

The `before` zeros are admissible because the control in the same command hits: the existing guard is alive and fires on the shape it was written for, and it still never fires anywhere on this repository's own declared population. The single `after` warning is the `dashboard` contest — no other key moved.

## 3. The predicate, derived rather than chosen

**Both tables, keyed on the declared full type.**

- **Both tables** — the one contested key on this tree is a stub in `lazyEntries` against a loaded registration in `components`. A same-table check sees neither side of it.
- **Full type, not loader identity** — nine bare keys are stubbed twice from two console files with two different arrow closures for one full type. Keying on loader identity would warn on all nine, at every boot.
- **Silent on the stub-then-real lifecycle** — the 30 agreeing keys, measured, in both orders.

⇒ the dispatch's live stop condition is **not** met: no first-party correct sequence depends on the silence, and the predicate that excludes the correct ones is exactly the one the census names.

## 4. Why `register` changed too, and why that is this card and not another

⚠️ Flagging this rather than burying it: the diff touches `register`'s existing guard as well as adding one to `registerLazy`. Both are inside the declared file surface, both are diagnostic-only, and the reason is measured, not stylistic.

In the order this repository actually boots — stubs at module scope, plugin chunks later — the silent overwrite happens at **`register`**, whose guard reads `this.components` only and therefore sees nothing while a stub holds the bare key. Ablation leg 2 below is the proof: with the `registerLazy` half in place and the `register` half removed, the test named for objectui#9533's own order goes red. A fix that added only the lazy-door check would leave this card's own measured instance emitting zero warnings at boot, and would report the contest only in the order this repository does not start in — the failure mode `report-bare-key-ownership.test.ts` and `timeline-bare-key-ownership.test.ts` replay both orders to prevent.

⛔ Nothing about what the registry ACCEPTS changed, and `skipFallback`'s behaviour is untouched — only what the registry SAYS. That is the `Clause-②: no` the claim declared, and the census did not push against it.

## 5. The warning text — written last, and the two doors deliberately differ

The filing seat flagged that `register`'s existing wording prescribes `skipFallback` as the remedy and that this may be wrong advice before a module has loaded. It is wrong advice — measurably, and only on one of the two doors:

- On **`registerLazy`**, `skipFallback: true` really does settle it: the stub then claims only `namespace:type` and leaves the bare key alone. The new message says so.
- On **`register`**, it does not. That door clears the bare stub *outside* the fallback branch, so it deletes the stub whether or not it takes the bare key — pass `skipFallback: true` there and the bare key ends up claimed by nobody at all. The new message asks for the two declarations to agree on one full type instead, and says why the opt-out does not settle this one. `skipFallback on the EAGER door does not preserve the stub's bare claim` pins that behaviour, so the advice rests on an assertion rather than on prose.

## Tests

All readings at final head `f502af2d`.

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/registry/__tests__/Registry.test.ts` — `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 49 passed (49)`; the 8 new cases were confirmed by name in `--reporter=verbose`, not inferred from the count.
- Registration sweep, one command: `packages/core/ packages/fields/` plus `registration-uniqueness`, `html-page-lazy-blocks`, `react-page-scope`, `react-page-state`, `report-bare-key-ownership`, `timeline-bare-key-ownership`, `plugin-map/src/index.registration`, `unfulfilled-chart-stubs-retired-8760`, `node-slot-registered-arms-8499`, `phase2-schemas`, `registry-bare-name-collisions`, `unit-registry-absence-collision` — `Test Files 333 passed (333) / Tests 6306 passed (6306)`.
- Second sweep: `apps/console` registry parity and chart-stub tests, `plugin-calendar` and `plugin-kanban` key tests, all of `packages/plugin-dashboard/` — `Test Files 124 passed (124) / Tests 1393 passed (1393)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check` exit 0, after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/core^...' build` (exit 0). The script runs `tsc --noEmit` **and** `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new tests are inside the typechecked set by construction.
- Gates, each exit 0: `check:registry-bare-names` (`237 bare key(s) claimed, 59 declined with skipFallback; 1 contested; ledger holds 1` — unchanged by this diff, as it must be: no registration site moved), `check:changeset-presence`, `check:changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check:test-path-roots`, `check:doc-types`.
- Lint, measured rather than assumed: `eslint --no-inline-config` on the two edited files gives 0 errors and 6 warnings; linting the BASE copy of each file gives the same 0 errors and 6 warnings, all `no-explicit-any` at lines that predate this branch. ⇒ **0 new**. The repository-wide run belongs to CI.

**Ablation — two legs, both against the committed fix, direction predicted and observed: TURNS RED.** Each leg proved its mutation reached disk (anchor matched exactly once, injected marker counted 1, blob hash differs from the HEAD blob) and proved its restore by an empty `git diff HEAD` plus a hash equal to the HEAD blob, with an empty hash treated as failure and an EXIT/INT/TERM trap holding an absolute repository path. No build is in this path: `vitest.config.mts` aliases `@object-ui/core` to `packages/core/src`, and the test imports `../Registry` directly, so there is no stale-`dist` channel that could keep a broken assertion green.

| leg | mutation | result |
|---|---|--:|
| 1 | the `registerLazy` collision guard deleted | **3 failed** / 46 passed — the two lazy-door cases and the remedy case |
| 2 | the cross-table branch of `register`'s guard deleted | **2 failed** / 47 passed — including `warns when a LOADED registration takes a bare key a pending stub claims (the objectui#9533 order)` |

⭐ Leg 2's red set is what makes the second half of the fix a measurement rather than an opinion: leg 1 does not cover that case, so the lazy door alone leaves the boot-order instance unreported.

## Acceptance notes

- **Not touched, deliberately:** objectui#9264's gate and its shrink-only ledger. This changes runtime noise, not the declared population; the gate reads the same 425 claims before and after and still prints `ledger holds 1`. Preserved from the filing seat and passed on unchanged.
- **Not touched, deliberately:** the `dashboard` contest itself. objectui#9533 is ruled and in flight as PR objectui#9803 (open, draft at 08:31Z). This card adds the detector; that card converges the key. If objectui#9803 lands, the single warning measured above goes away and the detector reports nothing on this tree — which is the correct end state for a detector, and the 30 silent keys plus the ablation legs are what keep it non-vacuous.
- `needs:contract-review` is the seat's to hang or remove; this PR neither carries nor requests it.
- No label was applied: this repository forbids the changeset-skip label outright and the claim assigned none.
